CRITICAL.description: Changes doctrinal meaning, reverses negation, omits a clause, or adds unsupported doctrinal claim
examples: Translation says 'there is suffering' where source says 'there is no suffering'
Omitting a verb phrase that changes the proposition
Adding a doctrinal claim (e.g., 'this proves Śaiva non-dualism') not in source

MAJOR.description: Grammatical error that misrepresents grammatical relations, wrong case role, wrong subject/object, wrong tense/aspect

MINOR.description: Stylistic preference, word order, synonym choice. Defensible alternative exists without changing meaning.
examples: Active vs passive if grammatical relations are preserved
